subject: URGENT: Demo Pod B outlet spark / aisle C internet drop — immediate triage

From: Venue Tech <venue_tech@venueco.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT - Small spark under Demo Pod B, breaker tripped (Aisle C)

Hi Alex / Monica,

Quick heads-up from the floor: at 9:05am our crew saw a small spark at the power strip feeding Demo Pod B (Aisle C). The local breaker tripped, there was a bit of smoke/tanning on the carpet and the demo table surface — nothing spread, we extinguished immediately.

Consequences observed:
- Demo Pod B is without power.
- Aisle C upstream network switch lost PoE briefly; multiple demo tablets went offline.
- ACME sponsorship staff reported the podium teleprompter lost power mid-run.

We isolated the circuit and shut power to that riser. We recommend an electrician and surge-protected temporary feed. We can supply photos and the breaker label. There was a burnt plug on a third-party power strip.

Attaching: demoB_socket_photo.jpg (stub).

Please advise on next steps — I can coordinate on-site electrician if you confirm.

— Mark (Venue Tech)

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 10:02 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> If the electrician signs off and power is safe we can restore podium power by 10:05am; if not, we'll run remote or move keynote to Aisle D.

Final update for the thread: thank you everyone for the quick turnaround. Summary: 
- Electro-Fix isolated the faulty third-party power strip, replaced the damaged outlet module, and tested the riser. No persistent wiring fault in the panel.
- Power to Demo Pod B was restored at 11:15am after electrician sign-off; we ran a 15-minute burn test.
- ACME keynote ran at 11:30am using the hot-standby laptop with UPS; their presenter opted for remote slides + video patch and finished on schedule. Backup speaker remained on standby but not needed.
- Demo Pod B will remain on a dedicated surge-protected feed for the rest of the event. We pulled the third-party strip and logged the SKU.

I've attached the incident report and added photos to the Drive. Please treat this as a record for ACME and our internal post-mortem.

Attachments: incident_report_20261116.pdf
Related: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-EventIncidents-2026, JIRA EVNT-2245

Next steps (owners):
- Monica: invoice approval for Electro-Fix (submit if >$250).
- Dylan: tag the demo kit and replace any suspect power strips before next event.
- Tessa: follow up with ACME ops to confirm satisfaction and offer a stand-down credit if they'd like one.

Thanks again — quick containment averted a longer outage.
